subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:05 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive.

Key pain points you described:
- High per-query cost for semantic search + reranking at 2M queries/day
- Unpredictable tail latency when trying to do cross-encoder reranks inline
- Need for structured, deterministic outputs for downstream transaction processing
- Tight data residency & SOC2 requirements for PII in embeddings

Goals we captured:
1) Reduce inference cost by ~30-40% while keeping top-1 accuracy for search/ranking
2) Achieve streaming responses for long-form assistant flows with <100ms token latency (p50)
3) Support function/tool calling with structured JSON outputs for your order-processing hooks
4) Maintain embeddings & reranking in-region for compliance

Integration / product fit notes (high level):
- SDK changes: recommend adopting Redwood's streaming SDK (client-side evented API) so you can show partial results while the model continues generating. We'll provide a small sample patch for your Node SDK to enable streaming and function-calling together.
- Function calling: Redwood supports function-calling with JSON-schema enforcement; we can return both a "tool call" event and structured outputs. That maps well to your order-processing hooks.
- Streaming + structured outputs: use streaming deltas with an explicit finalization event so your parser can be deterministic (we'll include example schemas).
- Embeddings & reranking: recommend a two-stage approach — lightweight ANN for recall (regional vector store) + a cross-encoder rerank stage for top-20 candidates. We can offer a managed rerank endpoint optimized for throughput.
- Security/compliance: we can host Dedicated capacity in your chosen region and support customer-managed KMS. We'll share SOC2 artifacts and the relevant penetration test results.

Attachments: redwood-sow-v1.pdf (initial SOW), integration-diagram.png, acme-eval-prompts.csv (seed prompts we discussed).

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive with Dev + Infra folks (60-90m) — can we schedule for next week?
- Redwood to send edited SOW + sample SDK patch by EOD Friday
- Share a small eval dataset (we'll run embeddings and a rerank baseline)

If that matches your view, I’ll schedule the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

> Marissa —
> 
> Appreciate the recap, this looks right. A couple of quick clarifying items before we bring our infra team into the deep-dive:
> 
> 1) Streaming: can you share expected tail latencies at 95/99p for streaming token delivery for a 3k-context flow? We'll need numbers to validate SLAs.
> 2) Function calling: does the function-calling interface allow attachments (we sometimes send a small binary payload to our order-processor) or should that be handled as a separate upload step?
> 3) Compliance: can Dedicated be provisioned in our us-west-2 account, and do you support customer-managed KMS keys in that mode?

Hi Samir — quick answers from the engineering side:

1) Streaming latency: on our Dedicated clusters with A100-equivalent GPUs and the recommended batching configuration, we've seen median per-token delta delivery under 50ms, p95 ~120-150ms, p99 ~200-350ms for 3k-context flows (depends on concurrency). These numbers assume continuous batching with prefix caching disabled for cold starts; we can discuss tuning for your workload.

2) Function calling & attachments: the function-calling payload is JSON-first. For small binary payloads we recommend a separate upload step (S3-presigned URL) and then passing the returned URL as part of the function call. That keeps schema validation deterministic and avoids streaming binary blobs in the token stream.

3) Dedicated + KMS: yes — Dedicated can be provisioned in your us-west-2 account via a marketplace/private offer flow. We support customer-managed KMS (HSM integration available on enterprise plans). We'll coordinate security review and provide SOC2 evidence.

Implementation note: for deterministic structured outputs, we recommend emitting a finalization event ("final_result") with a strict JSON schema and using streaming only for partial/preview tokens. We'll add a small Node/Java example for enforcing the schema client-side.

I'll attach a short integration diagram and a sample SDK patch before EOD.

—Dev

dev.patel@redwood.com
